newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Antitrust not happy with cordless phone plan.
newsitem.headline: Italy Antitrust not happy with cordless phone plan.

text.p: Italy's Antitrust watchdog criticised Telecom Italia's plan to launch an advanced cordless phone, warning of potential obstacles to the development of competition in the sector.
Telecom Italia, the country's state telephone company, last week unveiled plans to invest 1.8 trillion lire in the new phone system, using the Digital European Cordless Telephony (DECT) standard.

Antitrust chairman Giuliano Amato has already said if Telecom Italia went ahead it would be taking advantage of its dominant position in the fixed-line phone market to compete head-on with mobile phone companies.

The Antitrust authority said in a statement it had conveyed its concerns to parliament and to the government. The watchdog cannot set up an inquiry because the system is not yet operating and can only express its opinions.
The body said it was concerned that there was no concrete framework regulating access to frequency bands and the right to use the relative technology.

It noted that Telecom Italia had a legal monopoly in the fixed telephony market while Telecom Italia Mobile(TIM), spun off from Telecom Italia last year, had a legal monopoly in the TACS cellular phone market and a dominant share in the GSM market.
Italy's other licensed mobile phone operator is Omnitel Pronto Italia, a venture controlled by hi-tech group Olivetti.
Amato noted that the government had not regulated cordless telephony but that Telecom Italia was effectively offering a mobile phone service.

"If confirmed, the entry of the public operator as the first and, for now, only operator in the DECT cellular telephony market could be, in the absence of a well-defined regulation of access to this service, an obstacle in the development of competition both in the cellular telephony market, now liberalised at a European Union level, and in the vocal telephony market, which is due to be completely liberalised from January 1998," the Antitrust statement said.
